title: Choose Lucent’s visual world
question: Choose the identity that should govern Lucent’s app theme, icon, examples, and documentation.

options.label: Optical Bench
options.lineage: precision optics, calibration targets, and instrument housings
options.thesis: Lucent makes hidden transformations inspectable by aligning source, dependency, and native output on one calibrated axis.
options.viewport: A bright desktop workbench uses one strong optical axis, a compact rail, and aligned source, reactive trace, and native preview panes; the icon is a lens cut by an L-shaped sightline.
options.risk: A literal reading of Lucent can feel like laboratory software unless typography and controls remain warm and contemporary.

raised.raise: One active-depth band makes hierarchy unmistakable without flooding the whole interface with color.
Every state change obeys a discrete, testable visual law rather than decorative animation.
The system is designed for daily return: durable rhythm beats launch-day spectacle.

options.label: Registration Overlay
options.lineage: compiler source maps fused with print registration and color separation
options.thesis: Lucent is the moment separate typed layers register into one exact native interface.
options.viewport: A graphite app shell layers offset source, dependency, and rendered planes that snap into registration; the icon is three offset corner forms resolving into a crisp L.
options.risk: Registration marks are familiar design-system material and need strict restraint to avoid looking like a creative-agency brand.

options.label: Deployable Fold
options.thesis: One local declaration propagates through a linked structure and deploys as a complete native UI.
options.viewport: A desktop canvas unfolds from compact Lucent source into linked component facets and a fully deployed application preview; the icon is a four-cell fold opening into an L.
options.case: Product clarity is exceptional because linked propagation mirrors compiler-managed reactivity; audience identification is less immediate than the optical instrument world.
options.risk: Diagonal geometry can fight dense desktop layouts if it escapes diagrams, headers, and transitions.

options.label: Living Transcript
options.thesis: The compiler explains itself as a continuous, searchable conversation from source to native output.
options.viewport: A keyboard-first workbench renders source, diagnostics, and generated output as one exact 80-column history; the icon is a luminous cursor nested in an L-shaped prompt.
options.case: Developer identification is immediate, but product clarity narrows Lucent to terminal tooling and conflicts with the all-day, non-neon brief.
options.risk: Its retro glow is the most direct collision with the stated visual boundaries.

options.label: Native Panorama
options.lineage: Metro typographic tiles and panoramic native navigation
options.thesis: Lucent presents native desktop structure with no decorative layer between state and interface.
options.viewport: Large lowercase section titles lead across source, state, and preview panes while live tiles expose compiler status; the icon is a single cyan tile interrupted by a black L.
options.case: The Microsoft-native lineage strongly identifies with the audience, but it says less about Lucent’s compiler mechanism and can read as inherited nostalgia.
options.risk: A familiar platform language could make Lucent feel backward-looking rather than experimental.

options.label: Dependency Depth
options.thesis: A vertical descent reveals progressively deeper compiler stages.
options.viewport: The compiler pipeline descends on one depth axis with the active stage illuminated.
options.case: The metaphor obscures everyday desktop work and asks developers to decode an unrelated environment.
options.kept: A single active-depth band now sharpens Optical Bench hierarchy.

options.label: Discrete Pixel States
options.thesis: Every reactive state is a crisp, addressable visual swap.
options.viewport: Compiler states occupy a strict tile field with whole-grid transitions.
options.case: Discrete state logic fits Lucent, but the play vocabulary weakens credibility for all-day desktop applications.
options.kept: Optical Bench adopts strict, discrete visual laws for every component state.
options.risk: Reads as a toy language or themed demo.

options.label: Daily Instrument
options.thesis: Lucent is a durable tool whose interface earns daily familiarity.
options.viewport: A fixed identity plate anchors a changing daily work surface.
options.case: Daily rhythm is useful, but the vernacular imagery has no clear relationship to compilers, C#, or native UI.
options.kept: Optical Bench prioritizes durable daily rhythm over launch-day spectacle.
options.risk: Feels ornamental and historically unrelated to the product.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished developer framework identity with restrained blue-violet accent, clean docs, and conventional desktop controls.
canonCard.viewport: A familiar sidebar, header, code sample, feature cards, and a geometric L monogram transfer directly into a conventional Avalonia theme.
canonCard.risk: Clear and credible, but intentionally difficult to distinguish from neighboring developer tools.
